Two asks to include in the MAP:

2) A short evaluation plan for a prefetched KV cache experiment (what metrics you need from us and suggested TTLs)

Brenda — thanks for the data and the ask. Quick read-through of your sheet looks reasonable. I sketched a concise unit-econ checkpoint you can drop into the MAP. High-level notes below; I'll attach a short preflight checklist and a suggested prefetch test plan after internal alignment.

Short answers first:
- Ballpark tokens/$ (hosted endpoint, nv4-like perf): ~400–600 tokens per $1 if we don't batch, ~1,200–1,800 tokens per $1 with aggressive micro-batching + prefix/KV cache hit-rate ~35–45%.
- Prefetch experiment goal: validate effective token reduction at 50% of traffic for templates/common prompts and measure tail latency impact when cache TTL=300s vs 900s.

Assumptions I used here (please confirm):
- Avg tokens/interaction: 4.8k (you provided)
- Peak QPS: 120 req/s, but steady-state expected closer to 60 req/s
- Typical batching window we can tolerate: 10–25ms (we'll propose micro-batching of 1–8 requests depending on tail SLO)
- Cacheable fraction: assume 30% of calls are eligible for KV/prefix caching initially; we modeled a conservative + optimistic scenario (30% / 50% hit rate).

Immediate next steps I need from you to pin numbers in the MAP:
1) A short list of the top 20 prompt templates or system messages you expect to be repeated (we'll use these for the prefetch set).
2) Confirmation on acceptable p95 latency SLO for interactive flows (currently you said <350ms end-to-end?)
3) Any regulatory constraints on data retention for cached prefixes (if the cache must be scrubbed per session we adjust the TTL guidance).

I'll loop David to provide a quick sensitivity table (tokens/$ across batching and cache hit-rate) and Priyom to propose the MAP milestone dates and deliverables for procurement.

On attachments: I'll share a small XLS with sensitivity columns and a two-week MAP timeline that calls out the prefetch experiment (prefetch_test_plan.pdf).

Best,
Neha

--

Brenda / Neha — following up with the requested sensitivity table. Quick summary in-line; I'll drop the spreadsheet to the Drive link Neha referenced.

Sensitivity summary (rounded):
- No batching, no cache: ~450 tokens / $1 -> per-interaction cost: 4800 / 450 = ~$10.67
- Conservative micro-batching (avg batch size 3), cache hit 30%: ~1,100 tokens / $1 -> per-interaction cost: 4800 / 1100 = ~$4.36
- Aggressive batching (avg batch size 6), cache hit 50%: ~1,600 tokens / $1 -> per-interaction cost: 4800 / 1600 = ~$3.00

Additional notes:
- We modeled token counts as linear; however prompt vs response token ratio matters for KV caching effectiveness (we get better wins when repeated prefixes are user/system instructions rather than long responses).
- Latency trade-off: micro-batching window adds ~8–20ms median depending on how bursty traffic is; that is usually fine against a 350ms p95 target.
- If Saviant needs guaranteed tail latency <200ms p95, we should plan for a hybrid routing policy: route 10% of traffic to low-latency reserved capacity (no batching) and rest to batch+cache optimized fleet. That will change unit cost and needs a small Dedicated commitment.

I'll upload the workbook: saviant_token_model_redwood_sensitivity.xlsx and the prefetch test plan PDF to the shared link and tag the MAP milestone rows.

Questions for Saviant procurement to close the MAP:
- Are you comfortable with a 30-day rolling TTL for prefetched prefixes in the pilot? (we recommend 300s–900s for aggressive prefetch tests, longer TTLs if data is static)
- Would you accept a canary where 10% of traffic is excluded from batching for a 2-week verification window?

--
David Kim
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

Brenda — looping in MAP deliverables and timeline so procurement has visibility. Proposed MAP milestones (two-week pilot cadence):

Week 0 (prep, sign-off):
- Saviant provides top 20 prompt templates and confirms p95 SLO. (owner: Saviant)
- NDAs/data access checks complete; RBAC to prefetch test dataset. (owner: Saviant + Redwood)

Week 1 (prefetch experiment):
- Implement prefetch set (server-side prefetch of repeated prefixes). TTL variants: 300s for cohort A, 900s for cohort B.
- Run with micro-batching enabled (target avg batch size 3), capture: cache-hit-rate, tokens saved, p50/p95 latencies, error rates. (owner: Redwood engineering)

Week 2 (analysis + decision):
- Joint analysis: sensitivity workbook, finalize tokens/$ and the recommended deployment plan (hosted-only vs small dedicated pool).
- Procurement approval decision and recommended commitment level (if dedicated is needed).

Deliverables for MAP:
- Sensitivity XLS (David)
- Prefetch test plan & results (Neha + Redwood eng)
- MAP one-pager with final tokens/$ scenarios and recommended next steps for procurement (Neha)

Target close date: 2026-04-28 (give two working weeks after pilot to review and sign). If that timeline works, we'll add these items to the MAP and I'll create the HubSpot milestone HS-5821 with clear owners.

Brenda — two quick asks to finalize prep: 1) confirm p95 SLO and 2) drop the top-20 prompt list into the Drive link. We'll then publish the MAP milestones.

Thanks,
Priyom
